svg.text: Where BNK sits in the VPC
bnk-agentcore-demo · vpc-06dbebcc9fe3e1bad · 10.0.0.0/16 · ap-southeast-2 · addresses and SG behaviour verified live
AWS-OPERATED · NO PACKET PATH FOR US
public CAs only, and our cert is
VPC 10.0.0.0/16 — everything in this box is ours to control
but they sit in OUR subnet.
That seam is BNK's to police.
the VIP is a secondary IP on the TMM ENI — plain VPC routing reaches it
The same f5-tmm pod, second NIC, DPDK over vfio.
That is what the host-device pattern means in addresses.
Pod IPs come out of THIS subnet,
Its own SG. Nothing else is in it.
bnk-data admits it on tcp/443 only —
no shared SG, no subnet adjacency.
Its second NIC is in the subnet
A secondary VPC CIDR, deliberately OUTSIDE the firewall's accept list.
Routable to the VIP (AWS adds a local route), so the packets arrive — and the firewall refuses them.
Same host, same SG, same port as 10.0.2.6. Only the source range differs, which is what makes it a test and not an assertion.
:80/:443 from the agent SG + ALL from itself
this, not routing, is what admits path 3
AgentCore runtime ENI → VIP → pod. Runs today.
AgentCore Gateway → Lattice ENIs → VIP → pod. Not built — needs a publicly trusted cert.
stranger in public-2, own SG → VIP → pod. Runs today.
Tested live: from 10.0.2.6 the firewall ACCEPTS (200); from 100.64.2.43 it REJECTS with a TCP reset (curl rc=7). Same host, same SG, same port — so the only
variable is the source range, and a reset (not a timeout) means the firewall actively refused rather than the packet being lost. That is the fourth refusal, proven rather than asserted.
